question: does the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model run through a layer-streaming engine on this machine, and is its routing decisive?
answer: yes to both. 510 GB of weights, 40 layers, one 32-token prefill, and a top-1 margin of 2.4947 -- 484x the reduced fixture's 0.00515.

why_the_margin_is_the_point.reading: the reduced V4.1 cells cannot close because a 0.82% layer-0 difference moves the token, and it moves it because the MoE's routing is near-tied on Philox-drawn weights. A trained checkpoint is not near-tied. This is the first direct measurement of that on V4.1, and it is what makes the shipped cells worth running: 2.4947 of logit margin is not something a sub-ulp arithmetic difference reaches.

what_made_it_work: CUDA 12.8 at /usr/local/cuda/bin. The system nvcc is 11.5 and does not know sm_120a, so every TileLang kernel fails to compile and the whole path is dead. The oracle tool's own recorded command already carried that prefix.
the Engram row gather: 202.76 GB of tables served by reading the 4 rows the call actually indexed, never giving either table a resident form
an Engram residency wrapper: Transformer.forward calls layer.engram(...) BEFORE layer(...), so the Engram runs outside Block.forward and its projections need their own materialisation window

a generic buffer re-materialiser sized from the meta tensors themselves, rather than transcribing V4.1's buffer set -- V4.1 has window_kv_cache and compress_kv_cache where V4 has one kv_cache, a different compressor state shape, and an Indexer with no head_dim
the release's own fp8 block size (32 for V4.1, 128 for V4) read from quantization_config rather than assumed
not_a_claim: not an accelerator token: this is the external reference comparator running the vendor's own pinned code (ADR-003 section 18)
one forward pass, not a generation: no multi-token sequence has been produced and the nine-cell matrix is unchanged by this record
the expert path is the vendor's documented FP8 recast, which is also what the shipped V4-Flash oracle records; V4.1's FP4 GEMM is not verified here
peak device memory was 94,072 MiB against 97,887 available -- it fit, but not with room to spare, and a longer context may not
